races.name: Listen To Track Radio Live / British EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Fitzdares Your Personal Bookmaker Handicap

runners_data.name: Aukus
runners_data.note: Held up for Ralph Beckett's yard, 25 days fresh and wearing a hood; placed once from two runs at Goodwood but his three recent runs show a consistent failure to quicken from off the pace, and in a steady-tempo race he will need to travel unusually close to have any impact.|

runners_data.name: Celestarak
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's gelding carries a fading-in-finish flag and has run four consecutive poor efforts at Goodwood at shorter trips; though naturally a hold-up horse, the congested rear means he'll be shuffled closer than he'd like, and his recent record gives little confidence regardless of position.|

runners_data.name: Semper Femina
runners_data.note: Ran just seven days ago over 1m2f at a softer track, which is a fitness positive, and Richard Hannon's filly has placed twice including a recent second at 1m3f on soft; her style is hold-up but she's versatile enough to sit midfield and her improving form makes her a legitimate each-way candidate if the pace holds.|

runners_data.name: Blackisthenewblack
runners_data.note: The confirmed leader and key tactical figure; Andrew Balding's gelding landed a comfortable win at 1m2f on Soft at Sandown last time and steps up in trip, and with no rival likely to dispute the front end, Darragh Keenan can control all fractions — his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that leading is not truly his natural role, but the race simply hands him the lead by default.|

runners_data.name: Flash Kozo
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's gelding is a genuine hold-up horse whose last four starts include an 11th and a 16th at Goodwood, and while forced closer than ideal by field compression, there is little in the form to suggest he can reverse those efforts even in a more favourable position.|

runners_data.name: Boilermaker
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's gelding finished second at Goodwood last time over 1m2f, which is the most relevant recent piece of form in the field; Lewis Edmunds rides and, although the horse's natural instinct is to come from behind, his Goodwood course form and improving figures mean even a mid-group position is workable over this extra furlong.|

runners_data.name: La Peregrina
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has finished no better than fifth in four starts this season, and her last effort at Goodwood was a 12th — the redistribution into midfield forces her out of the rear-group comfort zone where she has already failed to register, making a big run here hard to envisage.|

runners_data.name: Darn Hot Dame
runners_data.note: The only other prominent-style runner aside from the leader and a notable profile horse: she won at Goodwood over 1m4f earlier in her career and Daniel Muscutt is a positive booking; if she slots into second off Blackisthenewblack's pace, she gets a lead-pony advantage over every horse behind her and her course-and-distance win is the standout credential in this field.|

races.paceDynamic: Blackisthenewblack is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m4f handicap and should lead from the outset unchallenged, setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop on Good ground at Goodwood. Darn Hot Dame is the only other prominent-style horse and will likely track Blackisthenewblack in second, leaving the remainder — Aukus, Celestarak, Flash Kozo, Boilermaker, La Peregrina and Semper Femina — to fan out behind in a compressed midfield-to-rear group. With pace controlled by a single horse at a steady tempo, the race will be set up for a thorough stayer who can travel within striking range and pick up over the final two furlongs rather than a deep closer who needs a breakneck pace to reel in the leader. This shape strongly favours horses capable of racing prominently or in a handy midfield position who possess the stamina to sustain their effort up Goodwood's undulating straight — true hold-up horses dependent on a fast pace to close into will find conditions insufficient. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate; Boilermaker, Celestarak, Flash Kozo and La Peregrina are all true rear-runners who are unlikely to get their natural position and will be forced to race closer than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blackisthenewblack Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Blackisthenewblack leads at a steady gallop and is never seriously pressured, dictating throughout.
scenarios.body: If Blackisthenewblack leads at a steady gallop and is never seriously pressured, dictating throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Darn Hot Dame sits a length off Blackisthenewblack and quickens past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Darn Hot Dame sits a length off Blackisthenewblack and quickens past in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Lets Closer Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Blackisthenewblack sets too slow a pace and ties up in the final quarter-mile, allowing a hold-up horse to burst through.
scenarios.body: If Blackisthenewblack sets too slow a pace and ties up in the final quarter-mile, allowing a hold-up horse to burst through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Field Bunches Midrace
scenarios.trigger: If a cluster of hold-up horses forced to race wide and prominent interfere with each other's runs, producing an erratic pace shape.
scenarios.body: If a cluster of hold-up horses forced to race wide and prominent interfere with each other's runs, producing an erratic pace shape.

watchPoints.text: Darn Hot Dame has already won over 1m4f at Goodwood and if she travels comfortably in second behind Blackisthenewblack, she holds a decisive positional edge over the hold-up pack — watch whether Muscutt settles her immediately behind the leader at the start.

Blackisthenewblack's STYLE_FIT flag is worth monitoring: if Keenan finds his mount unusually free in front or unable to sustain the effort in the straight, the race could unravel quickly for the front-runner and hand the initiative to Darn Hot Dame.

The cluster of five redistributed hold-up horses — Celestarak, Flash Kozo, Boilermaker, La Peregrina and Aukus — will all be jostling for a similar mid-to-rear position; watch for traffic congestion entering the straight, which could compromise even the best-credentialled among them.

Boilermaker's recent Goodwood second makes him the most interesting of the hold-up types; watch whether Lewis Edmunds elects to place him closer to the pace than usual, given how steady the gallop is likely to be.

Semper Femina ran just seven days ago and horses returning quickly for Hannon can arrive cherry-ripe; watch her market move as a guide to whether the stable is confident she has bounced out of her last run in good order.

races.name: Goodwood Horseracing Club Young Persons Membership Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Analogical
runners_data.note: Won over C&D (1/12f/GOO) and has proven course form at Goodwood; Sir Mark Prescott's yard sent her out 29 days ago and she maps as the race's controlling influence — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects she is stepping up in distance relative to her style niche, but she is the class act in this field and her front-running role is entirely natural here.

runners_data.name: Masterinthewoods
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f at Goodwood last time and Emma Lavelle is in decent form (T14: 2/6); steps up to 1m4f for the first time which is the key question, but his prominent style suits a race where he can sit just behind a non-pressured leader and pick his moment.

runners_data.name: Zikany
runners_data.note: 590-day absence is a significant flag and the trainer has no 14-day form to offer confidence (T14: 0/8); races from hold-up position and those recent runs over 1m6f in soft ground at Hea/Hea suggest she finds this shorter and firmer test unfamiliar, though two wins at 1m6f show stamina in abundance if fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Nowshesdancing
runners_data.note: Only three career runs so form is very thin; the step up from 1m in her short form string to 1m4f is unexplored territory, and while Harry Eustace's yard is active (T14: 2/21), the limited evidence makes this a speculative play in a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Galaxy Wonder
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's yard is firing (T14: 13/61) and Galaxy Wonder has placed regularly at this level, but she is a genuine front-runner type whose preferred position is crowded out here — she will likely push forward but cannot guarantee getting to the front, which tempers her chance despite the strong trainer angle.

runners_data.name: Damascus Steel
runners_data.note: Arnolda's yard has no 14-day momentum (T14: 0/5) and this horse's C&D run of 6/12f/GOO last time out is not encouraging; naturally wants to race prominently but with the front row already occupied the horse is effectively racing a position and a half off his ideal slot, making it hard to see him winning from an out-of-role spot.

runners_data.name: Gallant Lion
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f at Goodwood last time (1/12f/GOO) which is solid course form, and drops to OR 69 with an apprentice (Ryan Kavanagh, 5lb) claim helping the weight; races from hold-up and needs the pace to set up a strong late run — the Ryan Kavanagh booking and course win keep him relevant despite the tactical demand.

races.paceDynamic: Analogical is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push her early, she should be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop over this 1m4f at Goodwood on Good ground. Masterinthewoods and Nowshesdancing are the other prominent-style horses most likely to secure early position behind her, creating a compressed, single-file shape rather than a contested speed duel. Galaxy Wonder and Damascus Steel are true prominent types at heart but cannot all slot into that position given the cluster ahead of them — Galaxy Wonder, at OR 72 with Tony Carroll's in-form yard, is the more likely of the two to actually carve out a forward berth, while Damascus Steel is likely to be shuffled further back than ideal. This sustainable, unhurried pace strongly favours horses with the stamina to grind past a front-runner who controls her own fate — prominent horses with staying pedigree benefit most, while genuine hold-up horses like Zikany and Gallant Lion get their chance only if the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Analogical Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Analogical dictates a steady-to-moderate gallop from the front and meets no serious early pressure, she can build the race on her own terms.
scenarios.body: If Analogical dictates a steady-to-moderate gallop from the front and meets no serious early pressure, she can build the race on her own terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Masterinthewoods or Nowshezdancing tracks Analogical closely and produces a decisive move two furlongs out before she can respond.
scenarios.body: If Masterinthewoods or Nowshezdancing tracks Analogical closely and produces a decisive move two furlongs out before she can respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough in the middle stages to set up a strong finishing run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough in the middle stages to set up a strong finishing run from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Shuffled Back
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses battle for position early and the race breaks up into an uncharacteristically strung-out contest at an irregular gallop.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses battle for position early and the race breaks up into an uncharacteristically strung-out contest at an irregular gallop.

watchPoints.text: Analogical is the only horse who wants to lead and if Poppy Scott (7lb claim) allows her to bowl along unchallenged from the start, her course-and-distance form means she could prove very hard to peg back — watch whether anything tries to pressure her in the first half mile.

Galaxy Wonder will try to push forward despite being mapped to midfield — if Tony Carroll's filly gets away cleanly and Myla Coppins (7lb) takes her into a prominent spot regardless, she effectively leapfrogs the pace map and the scenario probabilities shift toward a more contested lead.

Zikany's 590-day absence is the single biggest uncertainty in the race; if Amanda Perrett has her cherry-ripe she could hit the line strongly from hold-up off a muddling gallop, but if she blows up physically after a long layoff she becomes a non-factor entirely.

Masterinthewoods goes up markedly in trip to 1m4f — his sole win at Goodwood came over 1m2f and it is worth watching how Joe Leavy rides him in the first half of the race; if he settles kindly he is a genuine stayer, if he pulls, the longer trip will find him out.

Gallant Lion carries the lightest weight (124lbs) with a 5lb apprentice claim and is the most recent Goodwood winner in the field — if the pace is stronger than expected, watch for Ryan Kavanagh producing him with a sweeping run in the final two furlongs.

races.name: Fitzdares Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Authorised Speed
runners_data.note: Veteran at 9yo with course form at 20f on Good at Goodwood, but sim-going record here shows no wins or places at this distance in similar conditions — prominent style suits the expected tempo, though the drop to 1m6f and a 769-day absence since last Jumps run raises big fitness questions.

runners_data.name: Maestro Del Mar
runners_data.note: Good trainer angle with Ismail Mohammed but has been off 209 days and the sim-going record is thin (0W0P); a natural hold-up horse by style who will struggle to find his usual deep position in a field with multiple closers, and the "fades in finish" flag is a real concern at 1m6f.

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Holds the strongest sim-going profile in the field (4W5P from 12 runs in similar conditions) and notably won over 20f on Good at Goodwood — the visor headgear and James Owen's 9/55 14-day record add confidence, and the hold-up style can be exploited when plenty of rivals are ahead of it.

runners_data.name: Crystal Jet
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner wearing a hood, with course form at 1m6f on Good and a win here in recent history — Toby Bulgin has a 0/0 14-day record which gives little trainer angle, and being the lone pace-setter at this trip on this track makes it the key tactical pivot of the whole race.

runners_data.name: Grilse
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan runner lightly raced (2 runs both on Good at Goodwood) with a hold-up style that cannot be fully expressed in this field; the short form string (75) shows no wins or places, and at 3yo carrying 127lbs there is scope for improvement but the redistribution away from its natural position is a genuine constraint.

runners_data.name: Pacific Storm
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's hold-up type has only one run, that over 10f on Good — the step up to 1m6f is a significant unknown but the trainer has placed horses well at Goodwood before; no headgear and no form depth makes this very hard to assess with confidence.

runners_data.name: Phantom Recon
runners_data.note: Unlabelled style (U) with only one run over 10f on Soft, so both the surface switch to Good and the distance extension to 1m6f are unproven; George Scott's 3/24 14-day strike rate is respectable, and being lightly raced means the market may reveal more than the form book.

runners_data.name: Tinkety Tonk
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's 3yo has a "fades in finish" flag and finished last (12th) on its only start over 10f on Good — the step up to 1m6f needs to unlock stamina reserves that haven't been demonstrated, and the hold-up style compounds the risk in a shape that may not see a hot enough gallop to bring closers into play.

runners_data.name: Treble Nine
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's lightly raced 3yo ran second over 12f on Good at Goodwood — the trainer's strong 14-day strike rate (12/65) is notable, Daniel Muscutt is an able partner, and the unproven style may well resolve to a mid-to-prominent profile that suits this shape.

runners_data.name: Koala Rose
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has placed twice from two starts (3rd twice, on Good at Goodwood and Standard at Sandown) — the consistent placing record and trainer's 8/57 14-day rate are positive signs, and the unknown style may prove to be a mid-division mover who handles the step to 1m6f.

runners_data.name: Make A Splash
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's 3yo has going listed as UNKNOWN with no historical runs recorded — there is genuinely nothing to anchor a style assessment to, and while debut/lightly raced runners can surprise in maidens, the complete absence of evidence makes this a speculative proposition at this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Crystal Jet is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push the pace, is set to dictate from the front over this 1m6f trip on Good ground at Goodwood. The pace will be sustainable rather than furious — a measured gallop that rewards those with stamina and the ability to travel comfortably through the race before delivering a late challenge. Maestro Del Mar and Grilse are true hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield only because the field's rear is overcrowded; neither is likely to secure the deep position their natural style demands. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting an honest but uncontested tempo — strongly favours prominent or mid-division horses with proven stamina at this trip and experience on Good ground, as the pace will not be severe enough to dramatically compromise front-end positions, but the longer Goodwood straight gives closers with class a fair opportunity.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crystal Jet Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Crystal Jet leads uncontested and sets a controlled, sustainable tempo that grinds out the weak and suits those travelling prominently.
scenarios.body: If Crystal Jet leads uncontested and sets a controlled, sustainable tempo that grinds out the weak and suits those travelling prominently.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Overhauling Late
scenarios.trigger: If Crystal Jet's lead is pegged back in the straight by a horse tracking prominently who delivers a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: If Crystal Jet's lead is pegged back in the straight by a horse tracking prominently who delivers a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Delivers Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely testing enough that the midfield gains significant ground through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely testing enough that the midfield gains significant ground through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts All Positions
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses bid for position early, the pace becomes messy and the race breaks up into a tactical lottery.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses bid for position early, the pace becomes messy and the race breaks up into a tactical lottery.

watchPoints.text: Crystal Jet's ability to control the pace completely unchallenged is the single biggest factor in this race — if any rival forces it to go faster than it wants in the first mile, its chance of lasting home is materially reduced.

Sixty Plus carries by far the strongest stamina profile and sim-going record in the field, and at 6yo with course form it could be dangerously underestimated if the market focuses on younger, less exposed rivals.

Treble Nine's second-place finish over 12f on Good at Goodwood combined with Andrew Balding's in-form yard makes it a lightly raced improver whose true potential is unknown — watch the market for any significant move.

Maestro Del Mar and Grilse are both natural hold-up types who will be unable to settle as far back as they need in this field — watch whether their jockeys compromise position early or get shuffled back regardless, as either outcome affects the race shape.
Make A Splash is a complete unknown on going and has no runs to reference — any significant market support for this runner should be treated as inside information and monitored accordingly.

races.name: Casamigos Handicap

runners_data.name: See Blue
runners_data.note: Course-and-distance placed form backs up the front-running role here, and Donagh Murphy's 7lb claim helps offset the weight; however the STYLE_FIT flag indicates this horse will be racing somewhat out of its natural prominent gear rather than as a true leader, which tempers confidence in a win.|

runners_data.name: Euston Hall
runners_data.note: George Downing partners a horse in career-best form — back-to-back wins including two Goodwood miles — and Ed Walker's 14-day record of 6/40 is solid; course form and recency of winning make this the standout prominent profile.|

runners_data.name: Politely
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at Sandown and a fifth here last time out suggest improving form, but Tom Queally picks up a horse with a relatively cold trainer 14-day record (0/1), and the 41-day break needs monitoring; genuine pace horse that should hold a prominent berth comfortably.|

runners_data.name: Queen Tamara
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse — Lewis Edmunds takes the ride for Harry Charlton — who has won and placed at Goodwood and recorded a course-and-distance win; Good ground suits, but from a wide hold-up position over a mile will need the race to genuinely be run to suit her.|

runners_data.name: Sponsor
runners_data.note: Headgear note (hg:t) flags a tongue-tie and a horse with a poor recent Goodwood record (10th here latest, 0 wins from 4 course starts on similar going); Brian Meehan's 14-day record is cold at 0/10, so this one looks a tough ask without a sharp turnaround.|

runners_data.name: Ciarrai Abu
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's 14-day record of 2/21 is modest, but Ciarrai Abu won impressively at Goodwood last time and is a natural prominent racer who will find it hard to replicate that front-rank position given the field's density of similar types; effectiveness here hinges on whether Kaiya Fraser can find a good early berth.|

runners_data.name: Mr Writer
runners_data.note: Won last time out at Goodwood over 7f and brings progressive form — James Fanshawe's 7/28 in 14 days is the best trainer angle in the race — but this horse is a genuine pace type unable to express its natural game and Daniel Muscutt will need to adapt tactics accordingly.|

runners_data.name: Annastarzy
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 6/57 is a high-volume positive marker, and Annastarzy's win came over course and distance last time; a natural pace horse remapped rearward because of field congestion, so Joe Leavy will need to be aggressive early or accept a compromised position.|

runners_data.name: Abundant
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance at Sandown last time and has multiple placed efforts at 8f — a lightly raced, improving type for Tom Ward; another true prominent horse squeezed out of position by field dynamics, meaning Darragh Keenan's tactical call early will be decisive for its chance.|

runners_data.name: Get Outta Here
runners_data.note: Won here over course and distance on latest outing, and Jack Doughty has a live claim; David Menuisier's 2/15 14-day record is moderate, but a genuine hold-up horse whose form profiles correctly for this shape — the one runner whose tactical style is not in conflict with its mapped position.|

races.paceDynamic: See Blue is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to push it along — the several horses tagged as redistributed prominent types (Ciarrai Abu, Mr Writer, Annastarzy, Abundant) are all natural pace horses who cannot all secure their preferred position and will be shuffled further back than usual, leaving See Blue to control proceedings at whatever tempo it chooses. On Good ground over Goodwood's mile, a single uncontested leader dictating a steady, controlled gallop creates a classic sit-and-sprint scenario: the pace is unlikely to be gruelling, the field will bunch, and the race will resolve in the final two furlongs. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all occupy that position, and of those, Euston Hall and Politely — with strong recent form and genuine course wins — are best placed to actually hold the prominent berths behind See Blue. This race shape strongly favours horses with the class to sit close to a modest pace and quicken off it, making genuine prominent types with course form and a turn of foot the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Closers Stifled
scenarios.trigger: If See Blue dictates an unchallenged, controlled gallop and the race is run at an honest but not searching tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: If See Blue dictates an unchallenged, controlled gallop and the race is run at an honest but not searching tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Injection Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the redistributed prominent horses — Mr Writer, Ciarrai Abu, Annastarzy — pushes forward aggressively early and forces a stronger gallop.
scenarios.body: If one or more of the redistributed prominent horses — Mr Writer, Ciarrai Abu, Annastarzy — pushes forward aggressively early and forces a stronger gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the leaders tie each other up, leaving a gap for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely honest and the leaders tie each other up, leaving a gap for hold-up horses to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If See Blue is allowed to stride off untroubled and the pace is so slow that no one can reel it in from behind.
scenarios.body: If See Blue is allowed to stride off untroubled and the pace is so slow that no one can reel it in from behind.

watchPoints.text: See Blue's ability to dictate fully uncontested pace — if any of the redistibuted prominent types (Mr Writer, Ciarrai Abu) pushes forward aggressively from the off, it changes the race shape entirely and removes the controlled scenario that currently dominates.

Euston Hall is the most dangerous prominent horse in the field with back-to-back Goodwood wins; if George Downing positions smartly in second and gets a clear run, this horse's in-form profile makes it the most likely beneficiary of the dominant scenario.

Several riders — Kaiya Fraser, Joe Leavy, Darragh Keenan — will be attempting to push prominent horses forward simultaneously from similar positions on the track; jostling in the first two furlongs could create an uneven pace surge that distorts the anticipated steady tempo.

Get Outta Here is the only runner whose race map position genuinely reflects its natural hold-up style; if the pace is at all honest, Jack Doughty's horse with a course win on the board could arrive late and be overlooked at a price.

Good ground is confirmed by the official going report across all races on the card — no deterioration flagged — which maintains the anticipated true-surface conditions that favour horses with Goodwood course form, particularly Euston Hall and Annastarzy.

races.name: Goodwood Horseracing Club Membership Handicap

runners_data.name: Akirra
runners_data.note: The natural pace-setter here with a win and place at Sandown over 5f, though her only Goodwood run produced a fifth; Clive Cox saddles her 22 days fresh on Good going which suits, and her OR=78 mark is workable if she controls the race entirely from the front — the concern is the STYLE_FIT flag suggests she is being asked to do a job not fully aligned with her deeper profile.

runners_data.name: Kesta
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly has form figures of 11/11 in her last two Goodwood appearances over 6f, suggesting this course is not her strongest venue; she drops to 5f for the first time since her 6f win on soft and the hold-up style in a race with limited pace to chase is a genuine worry, though Rhys Clutterbuck keeps the ride.

runners_data.name: Havana Smile
runners_data.note: Won over 5f here at Goodwood last time and placed over the same C&D, giving her the most relevant form in the race; she is a genuine closer by nature — placed at the rear of the map only because the field is stacked with hold-up types — so securing a good tracking position behind what could be a one-dimensional pace may be the key challenge for Tom Queally.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Consistent placer over this course and distance with three top-four finishes at Goodwood in five runs; Ryan Kavanagh's 5lb claim is useful off OR=77 but a 14-day turnaround and a wide draw in a field where the pace is not expected to be strong enough to stretch the leader is a limiting factor for a true hold-up horse.

runners_data.name: Duskaura
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's filly has been off 80 days and comes back over the same 5f Goodwood trip where she finished eighth last time; her most recent wins came on softer ground and she operates most naturally from the rear — pushed forward by redistribution only — making it harder to assess how she performs racing against her instincts.

runners_data.name: Carefree Dream
runners_data.note: J S Moore's yard has zero winners in the last 14 days (0/22) which is a clear form concern, and the 7-day turnaround following a Goodwood run is short; she has won at 5f on soft and placed on soft over this trip, but her best form came on softer going and she is another natural hold-up type operating out of her comfort zone in this pace map.

runners_data.name: Too Darn Good
runners_data.note: Henry Candy fits the hood today and the yard has shown 2/14 in the last fortnight — modest but not completely cold; a genuine hold-up horse whose best Goodwood and Sandown efforts came when pace was truly strong, and without that tempo she is likely to find herself flat-footed over 5f with the lid on.

runners_data.name: Red Snapper
runners_data.note: Kathy Turner's filly is the most course-consistent horse in the field with four of five runs at Goodwood all producing places or wins, and her prominent style makes her the natural partner for the pace shape this race sets up; the hood is unchanged and Ben Ffrench Davis (5) rode her to a placing last time, giving her the best tactical alignment of any runner against the projected race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Akirra is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Goodwood handicap and, with no other natural pace-setter to press her, she should stride into a clear lead from the gates and control the tempo entirely on her own terms. Red Snapper is the one prominent-type with any plausible claim to tracking her, and with Good ground and a genuinely sustainable gallop, the front end should enjoy a clean, uncontested lead. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically operate from the rear — Havana Smile, Duskaura, Carefree Dream and Too Darn Good are all true closers but are mapped forward because there are simply too many of them to all settle naturally at the back, meaning the hold-up shape is crowded and compromised. A lone front-runner on a flat, sharp 5f track with Good underfoot and no pace rival to force a scramble is the dominant shape here — horses able to race close to or just behind a controlled pace are best positioned, and the profile that benefits most clearly is the on-pace or close-tracking runner who can capitalise on a steady-to-moderate gallop without having to make up ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Akirra Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Akirra breaks cleanly, settles in front without a serious early challenger, and dictates a sustainable but not slow gallop.

watchPoints.text: Akirra breaks cleanly — if she leads by more than a length inside the first furlong with no challenger visible, the prominent and on-pace runners (Red Snapper, Havana Smile) are immediately under pressure to close a potentially widening gap over only 5f.

Havana Smile's draw and early positioning will be critical — she is a true hold-up horse forced into an earlier-than-ideal map slot, and if she ends up boxed wide or unable to find a clean run at the two-furlong pole her Goodwood course record becomes irrelevant.
One And Gone's 14-day turnaround and trainer strike rate of just 1/49 in 14 days warrants caution — even if the race falls her way shape-wise, the yard form dampens expectations significantly.

Red Snapper is the one horse whose natural style, course form and projected race position all align simultaneously — watch whether she can tuck in directly behind Akirra and whether the jockey times the challenge to coincide with the leader's natural drop-off point inside the final furlong.

Carefree Dream (7-day return, cold yard) and Too Darn Good (hood, no wins in good going) represent the lowest-probability closers in the field — monitor their starting prices for any unexpected market support that might signal stable confidence not visible in the public form.
